BIS Hanoi students achieve outstanding academic results, significantly exceeding world averages in renowned qualifications including IGCSEs and the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme.

All of our IGCSE students for 2026 have once again demonstrated exceptional success, both collectively and individually.
With an incredible 43% of grades awarded A* to A (compared to 23.1% in England) and 89% of grades reaching A* to C (compared to 55.5% in England), our students have once again raised the bar for academic achievement at BIS Hanoi.

In 2026, our students have secured an impressive 35.11 average point score in the IB Diploma, placing them among the very best students in the world.

62.9 percent of the cohort also received the much-coveted Bilingual Diploma, showcasing their linguistic prowess in two or more languages.

content.text:
**Short answer:** BIS Hanoi appears to be a well-regarded, academically strong international school and is worth considering—especially if you want a British-style education leading to IGCSEs and the IB Diploma. But whether it’s right for your child depends on fit, location, and budget, not reputation alone.

**What looks strong**
- Its published IB results are above the world average: the school reports a 35.11 average for 2026, compared with a 30.88 global average. Treat school-published figures as one indicator, not a guarantee of what an individual student will achieve.
- BIS is reported to hold Council of International Schools and WASC accreditation and is authorised to offer the IB Diploma.
- Independent school guides describe it as among Hanoi’s stronger international-school options, with broad extracurricular offerings and a settled community. Online reviews are anecdotal, so it’s worth speaking directly with current families.

**The main trade-offs**
- **Cost:** published 2026–27 tuition runs from about **VND 657.6 million in Year 1 to VND 970.2 million in Years 12–13**. Fees include items such as lunch, uniforms, learning materials, some activities, and secondary exam fees, but check the school’s fee schedule for any extra charges.
- **Curriculum and style:** its British-to-IB pathway may suit a child who thrives in a structured international environment. It may be less suitable if you want a different curriculum, a smaller or less formal setting, or a particularly local-language-focused education.
- **Location and commute:** the school is in Long Bien, so the daily journey could materially affect your child’s experience.

**My practical recommendation:** Put BIS on your shortlist, but visit before deciding. Ask to observe a class, meet the relevant year-group leader, and speak with parents whose children are a similar age to yours. Also ask about class sizes, support for English-language learners and additional learning needs, student wellbeing, staff turnover, and the full cost of attendance. If those answers and the commute feel right for your family, its reputation and academic track record make it a credible choice.
